about.title: About Water Intake Calculator - Daily Hydration Needs
about.description: The Water Intake Calculator estimates daily water intake based on weight, activity level, and environmental factors. Water needs vary based on body size, physical activity, climate, and health conditions. Use the result as a general hydration reference rather than an individualized medical recommendation.

faq.q: How much water should I drink daily?
faq.a: A common general reference is around 2-2.5 liters per day for many adults, but water needs vary based on weight, activity level, climate, diet, and health conditions. The calculator provides formula-based estimates to help you review different scenarios.

faq.q: Does coffee and tea count toward water intake?
faq.a: Yes, caffeinated beverages can contribute to total fluid intake, though many people still use plain water as their main hydration source. Review caffeine intake separately if you are sensitive to it or have health-specific guidance to follow.

faq.q: How do I know if I'm properly hydrated?
faq.a: People often use thirst, urine color, activity level, and overall comfort as general hydration signals, but these indicators are not a substitute for medical advice. If hydration is a health concern for you, consult a qualified healthcare provider.

faq.q: Should I drink more water when exercising?
faq.a: Many people increase fluid intake before, during, and after exercise, especially in hot conditions or during longer sessions. The right amount varies by sweat rate, duration, intensity, and environment, so use the calculator as a starting reference rather than a strict rule.
